description:
Evidence: on the distiller, job gates are evaluated 4,896 times for 2,141 distinct jobs (max 6 for one job); on fixture 00181, 140 times for 60 jobs. The prune inside the transport-layout gate walk is already once per executable (memoized on ExecutableFacts), so the repetition is the gate walk itself.

Mechanism: Job::missing_gates is re-evaluated at every pop_runnable and demand_producer_if_needed, and each evaluation of a transport-layout gate rebuilds the position recipes (NamingWalk over the executable's positions). Nothing remembers that a job's inputs have not changed since the last evaluation.

Related case: a grounded closure call names both its callee and its grounded return recipe as gates (recipe_positions in jobs/transport_layouts.rs), because which of the two the evaluation takes depends on the callee's evaluated layout. The gate is a superset of what the run reads.

Acceptance: one gate evaluation per job per change of its inputs, measured by a counter (distiller evaluations and 00181 evaluations before and after); the grounded closure call gates on what the run will read.
title: A job's gates are stated once
